purpose: Identify which listed source cruises may contribute multibeam soundings to the frozen 1 km H10N1 window without comparing morphology or inferring source contribution from the composite grid alone.

JR53_AMT11.archive_evidence: BODC cruise metadata and AMT11 report state EM120/TOPAS were collected through the cruise; after the MAR survey a single opportunistic multibeam line crossed the SW flank of Ascension while remaining more than 12 nautical miles offshore.
JR53_AMT11.relation_to_H10N1: H10N1 is not proven to lie inside this single SW-flank swath. Exact track/sounding footprint is still required.

JR287.archive_evidence: Cruise report states the EM122 was run continually through JR287. Cruise timetable shows transit north from Tristan da Cunha region and arrival at Ascension Island on 6 June 2013.
JR287.relation_to_H10N1: A transit/acquisition path near Ascension is plausible but no public machine-readable track or sounding footprint intersecting the frozen 1 km H10N1 window has yet been recovered.

JR15001.instrument: Kongsberg EM122 multibeam for Ascension survey; continuous swath bathymetry reported during cruise
JR15001.archive_evidence: Cruise report states a comprehensive swath bathymetry survey around Ascension. Event log: Station 47 at -7.1168,-14.7561 departed on passage; Station 48 at -7.8580,-14.4416; Ascension swath survey began 2015-10-14 13:31 at -7.8584,-14.4413 and completed 2015-10-18 13:30 at -7.9976,-14.3587.
JR15001.relation_to_H10N1: Survey-start position is approximately 4-5 km from frozen H10N1 and the preceding transit centerline is also close enough to make JR15001 the highest-priority source candidate. However the published ecological mapping is described mainly for 100-1100 m, while H10N1 composite depth is about 1928 m; therefore proximity is not accepted as source contribution.

JR16_NG.instrument: Kongsberg EM122 1 degree x 1 degree multibeam
JR16_NG.archive_evidence: 2017 Ascension/Seamount work is independently documented. IHO supporting material for Young Seamount records JR16-NG, EM122, Seapath 320+ navigation and 0.5-1.5 km survey track spacing. Later publications state 2015 and 2017 RRS James Clark Ross cruises collected multibeam around Ascension and offshore seamounts.
JR16_NG.relation_to_H10N1: No recovered public track polygon yet proves coverage of the frozen H10N1 1 km window; known Young Seamount survey is far from H10N1 and cannot be used as proof of island-flank coverage.

JR16NG_PLOS_2025_multibeam.description: Multibeam bathymetry of Grattan, Young and Harris Stewart Seamounts collected May-June 2017

lineage_gate.reason: The composite dataset lists four cruises globally but does not encode per-cell source attribution. Public reports establish acquisition context, not exact source contribution to H10N1.
